headline: Congress authorized a Justice Department block grant program that funds local partnerships to reduce crime in neighborhoods.
what_it_does: The law creates the Project Safe Neighborhoods Block Grant Program within the Department of Justice. Grants support local plans to reduce crime, evidence-based prevention and intervention programs, and data collection on results. Grant funds must be controlled locally to the greatest extent practicable, and 30% of grant money must go to gang task forces in areas with significant or growing levels of violent crime, firearm offenses, and drug or human trafficking by criminal or transnational groups.

who_it_affects.group: Local governments and community partners that apply for grants
who_it_affects.how: They can receive federal funds to write comprehensive crime-reduction plans, run prevention or intervention programs, and track outcomes.

who_it_affects.group: Gang task forces in regions with high levels of organized violent and trafficking crime
who_it_affects.how: At least 30% of the grant money available is set aside for them.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of communities that receive grants
who_it_affects.how: Local programs funded under the law may change the crime-prevention services available in their neighborhoods.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 18, 2018. The summary does not list a separate start date for the grants or the dollar amounts authorized.
